evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` check only verifies nonzero, unequal PIDs and nonempty, unequal invocation IDs. It never compares the `boot_id` in `manager.before` and `manager.after`, so a guest reboot between the two snapshots can satisfy the predicate without proving an isolated manager restart. The reboot checks use `boot_id` from the same snapshot shape, so requiring equal nonempty manager-phase boot IDs is a small compatible correctness fix, not a new protection requirement.
